sample_unit: participants (planned 100 users and 50 clinicians; 55 recruited so far)

links.outcome: Harmful responses in simulated scenarios and whether the AI supervisor corrected them
links.effect: In about 500 scenarios, Socrates 2.0 gave harmful responses in under 1% of cases, and the AI supervisor promptly corrected the dialogue each time.
links.quote: Moreover, tests in approximately 500 scenarios showed that Socrates 2.0 engaged in harmful responses in under 1% of cases, with the AI supervisor promptly correcting the dialogue each time.

unlisted_practices: Multiagent LLM architecture with an AI supervisor and an AI rater giving automated feedback to reduce looping and improve dialogue quality

screen.reason: Protocol describing the development and planned mixed-methods feasibility/usability testing of Socrates 2.0 (a multi-agent LLM tool for Socratic dialogue in CBT) with users and clinicians, reporting preliminary testing metrics.
